en.headline: Customs seizes live cat valued at HK$25,000 at Lok Ma Chau; mainland man arrested
en.dek: Officers intercepted a 61-year-old incoming passenger at the Spur Line Control Point on Sunday and found the animal in his personal luggage; the case was referred to the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation…
body: Hong Kong Customs detected a suspected case of illegal importation of an animal at the Lok Ma Chau Spur Line Control Point on Sunday, seizing one live cat with an estimated market value of about HK$25,000.

Customs officers intercepted a 61-year-old incoming Mainland male passenger at the arrival hall. Upon examination, a live cat was found in his personal belongings and he was arrested. The case has been handed over to the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department for follow-up investigation.

Customs reminded the public that importing animals into Hong Kong without a valid permit is an offence. Under the Rabies Regulation, anyone found guilty of illegally importing animals, carcasses or animal products is liable to a maximum fine of HK$50,000 and imprisonment for one year.

zh.headline: 海關落馬洲檢活貓市值約2.5萬 61歲內地男客被捕
zh.dek: 關員周日在支線管制站入境大堂截查一名61歲抵港內地男旅客，於其個人行李內發現一隻懷疑非法進口活貓，隨即拘捕，案件交漁護署跟進。
body: 香港海關周日在落馬洲支線管制站偵破一宗懷疑非法進口動物案件，檢獲一隻懷疑非法進口活貓，估計市值約2.5萬元。
關員在入境大堂截查一名61歲抵港內地男旅客，經檢查後在其個人行李內發現該活貓，隨即拘捕該名旅客。案件已轉交漁農自然護理署跟進調查。
海關提醒市民，任何人未領有有效許可證而將動物輸入香港即屬違法。根據《狂犬病規例》，任何人非法輸入動物、動物屍體或動物產品，一經定罪，最高可被判罰款5萬元及監禁一年。
